seen_candidates.understanding: The supplied continuation establishes the missing leader-to-FSM path: leaderLoop samples the commitment index, selects committed inflight futures by log index, passes the last selected index and future map to processLogs, and removes those futures from inflight ownership. processLogs prepares ordered tuples, and runFSM applies them through single or filtered batch delivery before responding. This supports a bounded handoff audit, including command and response identity. It does not establish eventual application, replication durability, or end-to-end correctness.

responsibilities.description: Accept client commands, collect voter replication support and expose commitment for downstream application.

handoffs.description: Commitment eventually permits FSM application and future completion. The producer-to-delivery path remains unrepresented; bounded FSM continuation reading is requested.

questions: How are commitment instances and startIndex tied to leadership terms?

responsibilities.applicability: Normal Apply processing; admission timeout and BatchApplyCh affect timing, and leadership-loss errors do not establish absence of effects.

responsibilities.description: Apply committed commands, correlate responses and capture application snapshots through single or batched FSM interfaces.

handoffs.description: FSM capture must provide state and matching index and term. The producer is outside the supplied runFSM excerpt and needs bounded continuation reading.

questions: How do filtered batch entries retain correct response correspondence?

responsibilities.applicability: Behavior depends on BatchingFSM and ConfigurationStore support. No batch-contiguity defect is asserted from the partial implementation.

claims.description: During normal leader command processing, delivery to the FSM must preserve the command selected under the sampled commitment frontier. A command's successful future completion must follow return of its corresponding FSM application call and expose that command's returned response, including when filtering entries for BatchingFSM.

scope.description: Safety of the leader commitment-consumption path from dispatched command futures through selection, tuple construction, FSM delivery and successful completion. Both single and batched FSM interfaces are included. Other log types are retained as filtering context.
assumptions: Main-thread operations are serialized as described by the supplied implementation comments, while runFSM may interleave with that thread.
Channel behavior follows Go send, receive and ordering semantics; no synchronized rounds or empty-channel boundaries are assumed.
LogStore retrieval supplies the requested stored entry on success. Storage integrity and durability remain unverified external guarantees.
A conforming BatchingFSM returns one response per supplied entry in the same order, as its interface requires. Whether library routing preserves that correspondence is checked rather than assumed.
FSM methods are opaque application callbacks. A returned callback is an observable library boundary, not independent evidence that the application implemented its state transition correctly.
excluded: Unconditional eventual application or future completion.
Follower AppendEntries delivery and snapshot installation.
Explicit user snapshot restoration and startup recovery.
Proof of replication durability, valid membership histories or commitment-report provenance.
A guarantee that an error future excludes later command effects.
Resolution of the BatchingFSM no-gaps wording or a complete Barrier audit.

grounding.derivation: Apply promises a future for application, the FSM interface requires commitment before application and return of the callback value through ApplyFuture.Response, and BatchingFSM specifies positional response correspondence. Observed code supplies a concrete chain from indexed logFuture objects through an index-keyed map and commitTuple objects to callback invocation and future response. The obligation checks preservation across that chain; the observed implementation alone does not establish compliance.
grounding.applicability: Applicable to normal leader-originated LogCommand futures. Filtered barriers, no-ops and configurations can affect routing and therefore remain behavioral context without becoming separately checked obligations.
unresolved: Commitment accumulator guarantees remain conditional on its actual input producers and membership context.
The full future interface documentation is not supplied; this obligation relies on the explicit Apply and FSM interface statements and does not define a broader concurrent-reader contract.
Shutdown can leave queued work unapplied; this proposal makes no eventual-completion claim.
The BatchingFSM no-gaps statement and filtering behavior require a separate semantic judgment.
conflicts: The logFuture structure comment describes waiting for commitment, while Apply and FSM interface statements describe application and application responses. This proposal attributes its stronger command-completion expectation to those public interface statements and preserves the comment discrepancy.
alternatives: BatchingFSM can complete several commands after one callback returns; separate callback invocations per command are not required.
Entries without local futures can be loaded from LogStore, while locally dispatched commands retain their logFuture objects.
processLogs may complete ignored non-command entries directly. That branch is not automatically a violation of the command-specific obligation.

grounding.derivation: recalculate advances the accumulator and notifies commitCh; leaderLoop samples that accumulator and selects inflight entries under the resulting index. This is a concrete producer-consumer dependency.

grounding.derivation: The existing goal concerns committed support for delivered commands. Checking preservation of command identity and the commitment frontier across the actual delivery path supplies one necessary contribution, without discharging the complete goal.

audit_question.question: Does the leader commitment-to-FSM path preserve each selected command and its future, keeping delivery within the consumed commitment frontier and successful completion after the corresponding callback return with the correct response in both delivery modes?
audit_question.importance: Clients rely on Apply completion and response values for a particular command. A routing error could apply an unsupported command, associate a response with another command or signal application before the callback returns.
contexts: Local Raft instance and leadership context

scope.description: A bounded leader command-delivery safety check retaining actual asynchronous handoff, both FSM interfaces and entry filtering. Begin at dispatchLogs with initialized leader state and represent later callbacks and completion as separate events.
assumptions: Main-thread state changes are serialized; FSM processing is independently scheduled.
Storage reads return the requested entry on success; storage and commitment provenance remain explicit unresolved boundaries.
Application callbacks satisfy their declared response-shape contract.
Correlation uses existing log index, term and future object identity within the local Raft instance.
excluded: Explicit user restore, startup recovery and follower delivery.
Unconditional liveness and a general completion deadline.
Proof of O_commit or G_apply as a whole.
Full membership, Barrier and snapshot obligations.

units.rationale: The newly supplied continuation closes the concrete producer-to-consumer mapping gap without requiring new source acquisition. One obligation checks the handoff while preserving commitment production as a directed, unverified dependency.

patch.rationale: Add one candidate obligation and one bounded unit for the previously unassigned commitment-to-FSM handoff. Existing claim meanings, assumptions and pending conditions remain unchanged. Responsibility entries retain version 1 and existing semantic text while adding the proposed claim and unit assignment.
gaps: Assigning U_fsm_handoff represents planned checking, not completed coverage or proof of the handoff's eventual-delivery wording.
G_apply retains unresolved upstream replication, membership and durability dependencies.
The newly visible snapshot capture producer has not been connected to the snapshot consumer in this task.
Batch no-gaps wording, complete Barrier behavior and non-command completion expectations remain separate semantic questions.
No executable model, checker result, calibration or implementation reproduction is supplied.

limitations: This is a proposal based solely on supplied materials; no tools were called or code executed.
The unit requires same-history correlation of actual command and future identities. Separate event reachability cannot establish its ordered handoff.
The finite remaining call budget does not cover the 17 pending inquiries. This proposal adds no additional reading request and does not imply those inquiries are resolved.
Responsibility handoff descriptions and accepted claim pending text retain historical uncertainties; the additive unit assignment does not silently revise those semantic objects.
